input.summary:
Full ledger built and traced. Authority used: input/disclosure.md plus the single substantive USER passage in input/conversation.md ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion"; "add autonomous mode"; "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand"). All other USER turns are operational resume/gate instructions and were treated as non-authoritative, as were the YOU turns and input/brief.md (used only for title, cross-reference "Not applicable.", government-support "Not applicable.", and claim-class policy).

Claims: all 20 traced. Claim 1 elements map to "a vibration motor coupled to a first side of a rigid base", "An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side", "The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material", "not intended to form a complete airtight seal", "restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile", "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter, maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere", "The resulting pressure differential holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward", "connected to the tile through rigid components", and "the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact". The "clearance along at least part of the perimeter member" is the minimal formalization of air entering beneath the perimeter while rigid contact is maintained, and the bearing face as the end face remote from the base is the necessary geometry of a skirt standing on the tile, not an added relationship. Claims 2-7 trace to the loop/skirt, the material list "plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials", the no-rubber-or-foam statement, the no-downward-pressure statement, "continuously removes air", and "such as a vacuum pump". Claims 8, 9, 12, 18, 19 trace to "one or more handles used primarily for guiding" and "a rope, wire, cable, or similar flexible pulling element". Claim 10 traces only to the USER autonomous-mode passage and is correctly location-neutral. Claims 11-15 (system) and 16-17, 20 (method) recite no matter beyond the above; the whereby of claim 11 tracks "decoupled control in which the operator controls position using minimal pulling force while the vacuum maintains consistent coupling". Antecedent basis checked for every "the" recitation across claims 1-20.

Numerals: all seventeen entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) carry one meaning in the description and in every brief that uses them, each appears on at least one sheet, and each sheet's header list matches its bullet list exactly (F1 10/12/18/20/24/36/44; F2 12/14/20/22/24/36; F3 16/24; F4 24/26/34/36/38/40/42; F5 10/24/36/46; F6 10/48). No numeral is defined in a brief without a description counterpart.

Figures: the Brief Description enumerations agree with the authoritative briefs for all six sheets, including FIG. 2's sectioned base/chamber/perimeter member/covering element with the air-extraction mechanism in elevation and the motor and handle omitted. Section designations repeat identically in the source view (FIG. 3 brief: numeral 2 at each end reading as line 2-2 leading to FIG. 2; numeral 4 at each end reading as line 4-4 leading to FIG. 4), in the resulting views (FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs), and in the Brief Description and detailed description. Depiction conventions (rectangular slab and ring, band depth, block order, the schematic gap through the slab representing the disclosed fluid communication, the pulling-element meeting place, the number and drawn position of the stirring elements) are each affirmatively hedged inside the figure brief only; none of them adds taper, angle, depth asymmetry, runout, radial or circumferential position, contact extent, proportion, or material, and none leaks into the application text. The application text carries only "shown schematically", "shown enlarged for clarity" and "omitted for clarity", with no "by way of example", no "any closed outline", and no optional embodiment added to justify a renderer's choice; the claims and description remain shape- and location-neutral.

Text quality: no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any of the ten sections; the detailed-description subheadings do not duplicate section headings; the abstract is 145 words. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the inventor, as directed. No unsupported or internally inconsistent passage was found.

input.summary: Full ledger built and traced. CLAIMS: all 20 claims (independent 1 device, 11 system, 16 method, plus 17 dependents) were traced limitation by limitation to the disclosure — rigid base with first/second side, vibration motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with the chamber on the second side ("An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"); rigid low-friction perimeter member and material list ("a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"); no-seal/no-rubber-or-foam and rigid contact ("not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam... maintaining rigid contact with the tile"); clearance and continuous inflow ("continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter"); sub-atmospheric chamber and hands-free holding force ("maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere... holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"); all-rigid vibration path ("connected to the tile through rigid components... substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"); slidability while held ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"); handle for guiding; rope/wire/cable pulling element and decoupled control; and claim 10's stirring elements, traced to the affirmative USER passage "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion". Antecedent basis, dependency, and claim-to-description term identity (bearing face, clearance, vibration transmission path, exposed face, pressure differential) were checked and are consistent. NUMERALS: all 17 ledger entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) are defined once in the description, each denotes one part across every sheet (24 = band/legs/ring/column consistently; 36 = tile/band consistently; 10 = whole machine in FIGS. 1, 5, 6), each appears on at least one figure, every per-figure numeral list matches its identification bullets, and no undefined or stray numeral appears in text or briefs; the 26-to-34 gap is permissible non-consecutive numbering. FIGURES: the six Brief Description entries were compared against the six authoritative briefs — cut bodies, elevation items, omissions for clarity, and schematic recitals match (including the repaired FIG. 2 enumeration, whose sectioned base/chamber/perimeter member/covering element and elevation air-extraction mechanism match the brief's hatched slab, legs and band plus unhatched housing). Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same repeated designation in FIG. 3's brief, in the resulting FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 briefs, in the drawing description, and in the detailed description. Depiction conventions (rectangular plan form, ring width, band and leg depth, block order and spacing, stirring-element number/form/position, port width/position/form, pulling-element attachment) are each expressly confined to the figure briefs; no convention, "by way of example", "any closed outline", or renderer-justifying embodiment leaked into the application text, and the claims and description remain shape- and location-neutral. Functional-surface statements were checked specifically: no untraced statement of deeper end, radial or circumferential end position, runout, taper, angle, or contact topology appears — the FIG. 4 bearing-face/clearance depiction is a minimally generic flat end face and gap over an affirmatively disclosed contact and leakage path, the FIG. 2 through-slab gap verbalizes only the disclosed fluid communication between the first-side mechanism and the second-side chamber with construction expressly disclaimed, and contact-versus-clearance section placement tracks the disclosed coexistence of rigid contact and air entering beneath the perimeter and the position-neutral "along at least part of" recital. TEXT: no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains in any of the ten sections; headings are not duplicated in bodies; the Field's autonomous recital, the FIG. 6 embodiment, and the Background's two-problem framing all trace to affirmative USER text or to prior-art characterization, which does not require inventor support. Operational USER messages (resume, regenerate, publish, audit) were treated as context only, not as technical support. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
